gap: No result ChatGPT got turns Lumary's beam angles into a common unit of light on the target. Spread over its 26° beam, the 550 lm 90°-tilt '355°+90°' model puts about twice the average beam intensity on a wall or artwork (≈3,400 cd) as the brighter 810 lm 40°-tilt 9 W model with its 45° beam (≈1,700 cd). Lumary's 6-inch 355°/20° gimbal has a 100° flood beam (≈2.24 sr, 4.7× the solid angle of the 45° beam), so its tilt barely aims anything.
standout_why: I compared against the cited lumarysmart.com 9 W, RGBAI Pro and directional-eyeball pages, the cited Best Buy L-GL4B4 and Wayfair 6-inch listings (going by how ChatGPT summarised them, because Lumary's store returned HTTP 429 and Best Buy timed out every time I tried), and our own dealectric.com page, which I opened on 2026-11-17. ChatGPT's answers already show the raw beam figures: a 45° beam for the 9 W and a 26° beam for the 90° model. What none of them do is make lumens and beam comparable, or say that the 6-inch has a 100° beam. Our current page lists '40°, 45° beam' for the 9 W only and does not mention beam angle for the 90°-tilt picks it recommends for art and walls. I could not source the beam angles for the RGBAI Pro and the Ultra, so I can't apply the normalisation to our current top pick. That is why this scores 1 and not 3.
decides: If the shopper wants to aim light at art or a wall, this supports the Lumary 4" 355°+90° (26° beam, L-GL4B4) and not simply the highest lumen figure: per lumen it delivers about 2× the beam intensity of the 9 W. It also pushes the 6-inch 355°/20° model (100° beam) down for aiming. Before our page can keep recommending the RGBAI Pro (sold as 'Pro Max' in the 2024 release) for 'aiming at art and walls', we need its beam angle from the maker page. If it shares the 100° beam that third-party manual summaries give the Ultra, its 90° tilt moves a floodlight, not a spotlight, and that recommendation would be wrong.
